close_reason: Implemented Option A across .5.1 (trait method MetadataBackend::get_metadata_changes with default impl) and .5.2 (MemoryBackend override extending ChangeEntry with ChangeRecord{ id, related_type, type_name } captured at mutation time, including destroy-time snapshot). Strict §3.3 conformance now achieved on the reference MemoryBackend; the default impl path documents the partial conformance for backends that have not adopted the override yet.
description:
Per draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01 §3.3, both filterRelatedType and filterMetadataType MUST filter the created, updated, AND destroyed arrays in the response. The handler implementation in JMAP-06zp.3.3 filters created and updated by re-fetching the objects via get_objects, but cannot filter destroyed because the objects no longer exist.

## Strict-conformance options

A. Extend MetadataBackend with a new method get_changes_with_filter(...) that takes filterRelatedType and filterMetadataType. Backend implementations would consult their change log (which already records relatedType / @type alongside each change entry) and pre-filter at the storage layer. Both server-side correctness and efficiency improve (no per-Id fetch).

B. Add a get_destroyed_metadata_metadata method that takes a list of destroyed Ids and returns (id -> (relatedType, @type)) so the handler can post-filter. Less efficient but no breaking trait change.

C. Document that under JMAP-06zp.3.3's implementation, filterRelatedType / filterMetadataType filter created+updated only; destroyed entries are returned unfiltered. This is a known divergence from §3.3 strict reading.

## Current state

Option C is in effect: handler-level post-filtering filters created and updated arrays; the destroyed array is preserved as-is. This is a pragmatic choice given:
- The spec defines the filter behavior in terms of 'Metadata objects whose [property] equals ...', which is ill-defined for destroyed objects.
- A client that wishes to perfectly filter destroyed entries can do so by remembering each Id's relatedType / @type from prior /get responses and filtering client-side.
- Backends that can do better (e.g. by carrying relatedType / @type in their change log) can implement Option A in a follow-up.

## Acceptance

Pick A or B and implement it. Update the handler to call the new backend method when one of the filter args is present. Move the post-filter unit tests to verify the destroyed array is filtered correctly.

Blocker for closing this: Mark's decision on A vs B.
notes:
Decision (2026-05-11, Mark): Option A — add `MetadataBackend::get_metadata_changes` with a default impl that delegates to `get_changes::<Metadata>` (preserving current handler-level behavior bit-for-bit). Backends that want strict §3.3 conformance override the method and pre-filter at storage.

Correction to the original bead description: `MemoryBackend`'s `ChangeEntry` does NOT currently record `relatedType` or `@type`; it only carries bare `Vec<Id>` for each of created/updated/destroyed (see memory.rs:89). Strict-conformance implementations need to extend the change log first. This is captured in child .5.2.

Decomposition:
  .5.1 — Add `get_metadata_changes` trait method + default impl; refactor handler. Non-breaking. No MemoryBackend changes.
  .5.2 — MemoryBackend override: extend ChangeEntry with (related_type, type_name) records, override the method, add destroyed-filter tests, clean up the partial-conformance note in metadata.rs:49-60.

Human label removed; this bead remains open as the umbrella tracker until .5.1 and .5.2 are both closed. Autonomous /do-beads loop can drive both children.
title: Metadata/changes filter post-processing — strict-conformance for destroyed array requires backend extension
